<thought>Based on the ESI mass spectrum, the most intense ion is at m/z 183.0451, which corresponds to a [M+H]⁺ ion. Subtracting the proton mass gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈182.0378 Da. The isotopic pattern shows a strong M+2 peak (~32 % of the base), characteristic of a single chlorine atom (Cl‑35/Cl‑37 ratio ≈3:1). Accounting for one Cl (34.9689 Da) leaves 147.069 Da to be composed of C, H, and O. The combination C₆H₁₁O₄ matches this remainder within a few millidaltons (≈3 mDa, ~17 ppm), and the calculated isotopic distribution for C₆H₁₁O₄Cl reproduces the observed M+2 intensity. Therefore the most plausible molecular formula is C₆H₁₁O₄Cl. </thought>
<final_answer>C6H11O4Cl</final_answer>
